summary_en: This study tests a combination of venetoclax, ibrutinib, prednisone, obinutuzumab, and lenalidomide (Revlimid), called ViPOR, in B-cell lymphoma that has returned or did not respond to treatment. The cancers listed include diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, Burkitt lymphoma, and non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Obinutuzumab is given into a vein on days 1 and 2, and the other four drugs are taken by mouth on set days. Each 21-day cycle is repeated for up to 6 cycles, or until the disease progresses or side effects are not acceptable. The main goal is to study the safety of ViPOR (Phase 1/Phase 2 study).
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa una combinación de venetoclax, ibrutinib, prednisona, obinutuzumab y lenalidomida (Revlimid), llamada ViPOR, en linfoma de células B que volvió o no respondió al tratamiento. Los cánceres incluidos son linfoma difuso de células B grandes, linfoma de Burkitt y linfoma no Hodgkin. El obinutuzumab se administra por vena los días 1 y 2, y los otros cuatro medicamentos se toman por vía oral en días establecidos. Cada ciclo de 21 días se repite hasta 6 ciclos, o hasta que la enfermedad progrese o los efectos secundarios sean inaceptables. El objetivo principal es estudiar la seguridad de ViPOR (estudio de Fase 1/Fase 2).
who_for: Confirmed B-cell lymphoma, such as DLBCL, transformed lymphoma, Burkitt lymphoma, follicular lymphoma, or mantle cell lymphoma
Relapsed or refractory disease after at least one prior treatment, as defined for each lymphoma type
Blood counts, liver, kidney, and clotting values within the stated limits, unless caused by the lymphoma
not_for: CLL or SLL (for the Phase 1b part)
Receiving another investigational agent, or chemotherapy, radiation, or anti-cancer antibodies within 2 weeks before the first dose
Prior treatment with more than one of venetoclax, ibrutinib, or lenalidomide, or allogeneic transplant within 6 months or active graft-versus-host disease
